domain: Historical Linguistics / Language Revitalization / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of the Hebrew language revival as a contested kernel where the commitment 'Hebrew is a living language' was read differently across two millennia. The liturgical-only reading treated preserved recitation as kernel occupation; the native-daily reading required reconstruction into ordinary generative speech. The contest centers on whether symbolic preservation counts as linguistic life or whether only native generation does.

key_entities: Hebrew language (kernel substrate spanning liturgical and vernacular forms)
Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and language revival movement (architects of native-daily reading)
Yishuv/early Israeli state (native-daily reading instantiation context)
key_tensions: Preservation vs generation (recitation of fixed texts vs productive native speech)
Sacred vs profane (liturgical restriction vs everyday vernacular use)
key_claims: Liturgical reading: Hebrew remained 'living' through continuous ritual use across diaspora
Native-daily reading: Hebrew was 'dead' until reconstructed as mother tongue in late 19th c.
Library verdict: D1 strict-reachability break indicates discontinuity in generative capacity
Both readings claim fidelity to the same kernel commitment
key_mechanisms: Liturgical transmission: ritual recitation, Torah study, prayer book preservation
Language planning: Ben-Yehuda's lexical expansion, grammar standardization, educational policy
State enforcement: Hebrew as official language of Israel, compulsory education
key_absences: Intermediate readings (e.g., scholarly-only, written-only) not surfaced in prompt
Comparative cases (Irish, Cornish, Manx revivals) that might clarify kernel boundaries

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The commitment that Hebrew is a living language, held as shared substrate across radically different interpretive communities
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Liturgical reading: rabbinic authority grounded in unbroken chain of transmission (mesorah). Native-daily reading: linguistic modernizers grounded in generative capacity and demographic fact of native speakers
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Tradition (Pattern 2) transitioning to Founding Text (Pattern 1) under native-daily reading

readings.commitment: Hebrew is living because it is continuously used in sacred ritual and study, regardless of vernacular absence
readings.authority_grounding: Rabbinic tradition; unbroken chain of transmission (mesorah); preservation of pronunciation and cantillation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constraint type: rope (coordination around fixed liturgical corpus). Beneficiary: rabbinic authorities controlling interpretation. Victim: vernacular innovation (suppressed as profanation). Base extractiveness: v_low (preservation mechanism, not extraction). Generative capacity: absent (recitation only, no productive speech).

readings.commitment: Hebrew is living only when spoken natively as mother tongue in ordinary contexts, requiring reconstruction of generative capacity
readings.authority_grounding: Linguistic modernizers (Ben-Yehuda et al.); demographic fact of native speakers; state institutional backing
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constraint type: scaffold (deliberate construction of new linguistic infrastructure). Beneficiary: Zionist state-building project. Victim: Yiddish and other diaspora vernaculars (displaced). Base extractiveness: moderate (requires suppression of competing languages, educational coercion). Generative capacity: present (native speakers produce novel utterances).

readings.commitment: Hebrew is living through continuous written scholarly production (responsa, commentary, philosophical works), independent of spoken vernacular
readings.authority_grounding: Medieval and early modern Jewish intellectuals; written corpus as evidence of productive use
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constraint type: piton (atrophied vernacular capacity, preserved written capacity). Beneficiary: scholarly elite with literacy access. Victim: illiterate majority excluded from participation. Base extractiveness: low (elite preservation, limited coercion). Generative capacity: partial (productive writing, no spoken generation).

omegas.description: Library verdict D1 (strict-reachability break) suggests discontinuity, but timing is contested. Did break occur at vernacular loss (70-200 CE), or was there continuity through written/liturgical use? Affects whether native-daily reading is revival or continuation.
omegas.source: Research context flag + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Extraction identified but did not fully explore intermediate readings (e.g., Sephardic vs Ashkenazi pronunciation traditions, Haskalah written Hebrew). These may constitute additional kernel readings with distinct constraint structures.

Irish, Cornish, Manx, and other revival cases not examined. Comparative analysis might clarify whether Hebrew case is structurally unique or instantiates general pattern of liturgical-to-vernacular transitions.

Under liturgical reading, rabbinic authorities are beneficiaries. Under native-daily reading, they become victims (loss of interpretive monopoly). This reversal may indicate tangled_rope structure not fully captured in individual readings.

What minimum threshold of productive speech constitutes 'generative capacity'? Scholarly-written reading has productive writing but no speech. Does this count as partial generation or zero generation? Affects piton vs rope classification.
